sections.transcript: Many of us will remember as children, waking up early Saturday morning, trekking down stairs while our parents slept, and flipping on our favorite Saturday morning cartoons, a weekend ritual that entertained children and allowed weary parents a few extra hours of sleep. Saturday morning cartoons seemed like a win-win situation. Indeed, despite their primary purpose being a means to advertise products to a young and captive audience for several hours a week, most parents likely appreciated the brief reprieve that they provided. However, Natalie Kingsley, spokesperson for the parent advocacy group Turn It Off, contends that children today watch far more than just a few hours of TV in a week. With most Canadian homes now owning multiple televisions, in addition to other electronic product devices such as computers, tablets, or cell phones, children now have access to round-the-clock TV programming and games. Kingsley believes the excessive time spent in these sedentary behaviors can be blamed for the increasing prevalence of disorders such as obesity and attention deficit disorder seen in children today. She also aptly points out the disturbing trend towards infant and toddler-specific television programming, such as Lala TV, which despite warnings from the majority of pediatricians that children under two should never watch TV, are becoming increasingly popular. Yet, for Maya Pang, a working mother of three, Lala TV has been a lifesaver. While Pang understands the importance of not letting her 10-month-old watch TV all day, she is grateful for the hour of quiet provided when her child watches his favorite TV show, a rare moment of calm that allows her to get supper prepared. Being a parent herself, Kingsley understands Pang sentiment. However, she asserts that although this one hour may seem harmless, before the age of three, children learn better from the real world. They may be fascinated and entertained by the images they see on a screen, but they are unable to make sense of them. Time spent watching TV takes away from time that should be spent exploring the real world, A fact which can have adverse effects on learning, in particular language development. While Pang is aware of these concerns, she believes parents can drive themselves nuts trying to be perfect. Letting her son watch Lala TV each day gives her the time to prepare a healthy, home-cooked dinner for her family. Before Lala TV, a fussy infant, combined with Pang's busy schedule, meant dinners often consisted of takeout or frozen meals. for paying, although not a perfect solution, it is one that works for her family.

paragraphs: Dear Ms. Alvarez,

I am interested in enrolling in Spanish language classes at your school and would like a bit more information. Having reviewed the course information on your website, I'm excited about the variety of special activities offered in your classes and would like to enroll for the next semester. However, I'd like your advice as to which course and level would be most suitable for me.

I have been studying Spanish at another local language school for the past three months, but I find that the teaching style is ineffective for my learning preferences. We are required to do a lot of self-study and are expected to teach ourselves the content before attending class. This is a real challenge because I have a full-time job and don't have time to complete the four hours of homework assigned each week. As a result, I often feel lost in the class because I haven't properly understood the content and the teacher doesn't explain it well. The manner in which the courses are taught at my current school is not working for me. The main reason I chose to take Spanish classes was for fun, but so far my experience has been stressful. However, I think that the curriculum at your school looks really fun and interesting, especially the practical exercises such as cooking, dancing, and watching Spanish movies.

I would appreciate your advice on course options. I'm looking for a class that focuses specifically on listening and speaking skills so that I am comfortable using the language when traveling. I have already studied the basics such as introductions and greetings, describing daily routines, and giving directions. After looking at your curriculum, I can't decide whether your Beginner Level 2 or 3 class would be most appropriate. I would really appreciate your advice. Oh, perhaps we could arrange an interview by telephone so that you could suggest an appropriate level for me. You can reach me by email at this address or by phone at 902-244-4444 in the evenings after 6 p.m.
I look forward to hearing from you!
Regards,

paragraphs: A. Matches made of wood splinters and dipped in sulphur, a chemical element, date back to tenth-century China. However, some Chinese scholars speculate that women may have invented matches as early as 577 CE, at a time when they were unable to freely search for tinder due to threat of attack from invaders. This "fire inch-stick" technology seems to have evolved separately in nineteenth-century Europe when, in Paris in 1805, chemist Jean Chancel created matches that burst into flame when dipped in sulphuric acid.

B. The next generation of matches relied on friction to produce a flame. These "strike anywhere" matches ignited when the tip, containing the necessary chemicals to produce combustion, was struck against a rough surface. Although developed in 1827 in England by a chemist named John Walker, they were commercialized by Samuel Jones. Due to Jones's efforts, these "Lucifers" became popular in various European countries and led to increased tobacco use.

C. In France, in 1831, Charles Sauria developed a new type of match made with white phosphorus, another chemical element. Effective even on rainy days and free of the pungency that assailed the nose when Chancel's and Walker's matches were lit, these matches gained mass production and worldwide use. Unfortunately, this next generation of matches was unsafe for the labourers who manufactured them: workplace exposure to phosphorus vapour caused deterioration of the jaw bone. Despite a workers' strike, a vigorous information campaign, and voluntary discontinuation in a few European countries, the majority of countries persisted in manufacturing white phosphorus matches until 1906, when the process was finally banned under the law.

D. Gradually, factory owners replaced white phosphorus with red phosphorus, a considerably less poisonous chemical that is still used in matches today. In fact, a single state-of-the-art match factory in Sweden produces millions of boxes of tiny matches daily using red phosphorus and wood splinters from aspen trees. The red phosphorus is mixed with powdered glass or some other substance to create a rough striking surface, which is then safely positioned on the outside of the matchbox containing the aspen splinters. Only when the match is struck against the surface will it ignite. These "safety matches" were developed in Sweden, in 1844, by Gustaf Pasch, although it was Joshua Pusey who invented the matchbook in 1889 as an alternative to the matchbox. Pusey's patent was challenged by the Diamond Match Company, which had invented a similar matchbook; the difference was that their striking substance was on the outside, whereas Pusey's was on the inside.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

paragraphs: Following the advice of experts, more and more health-conscious consumers are consuming fish at least twice a week for the heart-healthy benefit of essential omega-3 fatty acids. Nutritionist Andy Veinot not only urges consumers to ensure their fish choices contain sufficient levels of omega-3 fatty acids, but also to verify that the fish is free of contaminants. Veinot adds that the latter is usually not applicable to Canada due to federal regulations.

Aquaculture, or fish farming, produces about one third of the world's seafood. Most of the shrimp, salmon, and tilapia found in grocery stores is farmed. "If we didn't have aquaculture, we wouldn't have so much fish available," says Maria Cordova, who prepares fish for her family three times a week. "Farmed fish is more reasonably priced than wild fish and is on hand at the market every day." Catching farmed fish doesn't depend on the weather or on government-set quotas, both of which affect fishing in the wild. Department of Aquaculture representative Marcus DeSilva argues that aquaculture helps preserve the ecology of the wild species; thus, overfishing and the endangerment of fish species are less prevalent. "Wild fish may have greater flavour, better appearance, and better nutrition, but farmed fish is more accessible and more ecology-minded," he says.

Critics of aquaculture are primarily concerned about contaminants. Fishermen control the diets of farmed fish and insert additives in the food. Veinot points out that this is where problems can arise. "The components of the food may not be healthy," he says. Angela Crispino, president of the Council for Aquaculture Reform, carries the argument further. "The fish farm environment of tightly massed-together fish in the pens causes greater susceptibility to disease and, consequently, the administration of high doses of antibiotics. This is harmful to consumers." Crispino adds that the water is usually contaminated, either from the fish themselves or from other environmental factors. Nonetheless, medical professionals and nutritionists maintain that many foods contain additives nowadays, but the benefits of eating fish far outweigh any perceived disadvantages.

Explain what the salesperson did for you.
Describe the positive results from the salesperson's advice.

paragraphs: Dear manager at Home Gardens,

A few weeks ago I came to your downtown branch in need of assistance regarding my private garden. I had a considerable problem with pests and weeds and was having a hard time maintaining the health of my plants. Although I enjoy gardening very much, I confess I was a bit lost on how to approach the situation.

Upon arriving at the store, I was greeted by Daniel, who was delightfully supportive and helpful. He inquired about my specific needs and pointed me to the products that he believed would help me most efficiently. I could tell that there were more expensive options available, but also that he was more concerned about making sure I would be satisfied with the results rather than earning a big commission.

After following Daniel's recommendations, I am happy to see that my petunias are looking much healthier. In fact, because he went the extra mile and gave me such insightful pointers, I have expanded my gardening skills and have even ventured so far as planting a few cacti! It would be remissive of me not to lend him my strongest endorsement to his superiors.
Regards,
Mary Smith
John Bean, the Manager of the Garden Center,

Few weeks ago I have realized that something was going wrong with my garden. Most of the flowers were rapidly dying, weeds were growing all around the place and were also attracting many insects that I have never seen before. I am still new to gardening so I decided to visit your Garden Center in order to ask for advice.

The salesperson, a young woman named Rose, politely suggested her assistance when she saw me helplessly struggling to find the right products on the shelves. She patiently listened to my explanation without interrupting and then asked few additional questions to find out how I was taking care of my plants so far. After that she passed me two bottles of liquids, encouraged to follow the instructions and assured that my garden will look much better after 3 or 4 days. Guess what! She was totally right! I got rid off the weeds and the flowers are growing again.
I am extremely thankful for her help and glad that you train your staff properly. Keep up the good work!
Faithfully yours,
Lucas
Dear Manager,

My name is Tom. Before three weeks, I went into your store for help. When I came into the store, your employee, John, helped me with my problem. He showed me everything I asked about flowers. We walked in the Garden Centre, and for any of my questions, he had good answers. John sold me the best flowers in the store and told me how to take care of them.
Now, three weeks later, my backyard looks fantastic. Finally, I got what I wanted. My neighbours can't believe how my garden looks!
I want to tell you, John is a very good man. You are lucky because you have a great person in your company.
Thank you for your time. John deserves a raise!
Tom!

tasks.title: Responding to Survey Questions
scenario: There are plans to improve your city. Two different ideas are being discussed. One is to build a bigger library with more computers and more books. The other is to build a new playground. The playground in your neighbourhood now is very small and old. The city planners want to ask the public for their opinion.
tasks.instruction: Choose the option that you prefer. Why do you prefer your choice? Explain the reasons for your choice. Write about 150-200 words.
options: Option A: I think the city should build a bigger library.
Option B: I think the city should build a new playground.

paragraphs: It is unfortunate that budgetary constraints allow for the improvement of only one of either the library or playground. Both are worthy of investment. Since, however, one has to be prioritized over the other, I feel that it is the playground which needs the most urgent attention.

Our town's growth in recent years - especially amongst young families - has resulted in the chronic overcrowding of this facility. Children regularly have to wait significant lengths of time to take their turn on playground equipment, which has caused frustration and lead to a number of arguments with those perceived to be 'pushing in'.
In addition, the increased wear and tear on already old equipment has caused a number of pieces of equipment to break. This is potentially dangerous to the young children who use the playground.

Spending money to increase the book stock of our local library doesn't especially add value to a community which has, as its fastest growing demographic, a population which is not yet reading! It should be noted that libraries have always been able to acquire unstocked books from other facilities on request. This community can therefore afford to wait for the planned library expansion.
I am very glad to have a chance to express my opinion about new city plan.
I think both of two ideas are very important for the city. I truly believe the new playground will be better investment for a few reasons.

First of all, current playground is very old and even dangers for the kids to play there. It was build 50 years ago and has never been renovated. The city has to rebuild or remove dangers part of the contraction to make it safe.

The second reason is the playground is too small for the amount of the kids playing there every day. Population of our city is growing very fast and we need to be ready to provide them nice, big and save place to play and grow.
I think the investing in to the new playground will be more important compare to bigger library investment. New generation deserves better playground.
Kate Smith
Nowadays, there many changes of quality of our life. Improving the city more, we can get a lot of new things from it.
In my opinion, I strongly prefer that city should build a new playground.
Firstly, playground make us very healthy. Recently the number of lucking exercise is increased.

If city build a new playground, we can play tennis, baseball and so on. The chance of exercising is going to be increased. What is more, exercise is good for brain. It helps our concentration with work or children's study ability as well because of blood stream.
Secondly, playground make our relationship better. We can talk each other. Also we can meet new people inside the playground. Communicate with each other and exchange something new information.
Lastly, inside of the playground, there are many natures. Natures makes us more relax. Also good for eyes. In the busy world, relax and take a break is the key to be health.
Hence, playground will be great effective for us.

prompt: You know that one of your co-workers, who is going to retire in a few months, has been stealing from the company. Your co-worker Sam thinks that you should not bother reporting the theft, since the man is about to retire. Another co-worker, Erin, thinks that you need to report the theft to your boss as soon as possible.
choices: Talk to Sam. Explain why you want to report the theft.
Talk to Erin. Explain why you do not want to report the theft.
